summary: Bulcsu Siklós worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of London under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski and teacher Charles R. Bawden, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

Bunga Fukui (1934–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Maxime Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1974–2005).

Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani, and was appointed lecturer of Tibetan at the University of Tokyo in 1951, succeeding Tokan Tada.

Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University, specializing in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He worked for the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, Tokyo National Museum, and became Director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at Otani University and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later serving in leadership roles at Otani University and lecturing at the University of Tokyo.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) studied at the University of Tokyo, specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He taught at Rikkyo University and First Higher School before serving as professor at Kyoto University (1906–1929) and director of its Institute for Research in Humanities (1938).

Burchard Brentjes (1929–2012) was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode (~1950–1954), where he subsequently held an academic post (~1954–1978) and succeeded Mode in 1978.

Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg. He was affiliated with the University of Hamburg (attested 1997) and served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burton Stein (1926–1996) was a historian specializing in Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1968–1983) and SOAS University of London (~1983–1996), where he served as Professorial Research Associate in the Department of History.

Burton Watson (1925–2017) specialized in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Columbia University under L. Carrington Goodrich, Chi-chen Wang, and Wm. Theodore de Bary, and at Kyoto University, he taught at Kyoto, Columbia (1961), and Stanford (~1964–1965).

C. D. Sebastian specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, completed postdoctoral work under Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and served as Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Kunhan Raja (1895–1963) was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a D.Phil. at Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Madras from 1927 and was Honorary Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre.
C. Peter Bankart is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with Wabash College (attested 2003) and served as a visiting researcher at Dartmouth College.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu (b. 1888) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College, and served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1913–1943).
C. S. Srinivasachariar (1890–1951) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held appointments as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. S. Sundaram was an Indology scholar who held positions at Madras Sanskrit College and the University of Madras, where he served as Reader in Sanskrit beginning in 1951.

C. W. Huntington, Jr. (1949–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti (1910–1983) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency College, Chennai under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held curatorial and leadership posts at the Government Museum Chennai, Indian Museum, Archaeological Survey of India, and National Museum, New Delhi.

Calvert Watkins (1933–2013) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard, EPHE, and DIAS. He served as professor at Harvard (1959–2003) and later as Distinguished Professor in Residence at the University of California, Los Angeles (2003–2013).

Cameron Bailey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed undergraduate studies at Indiana University, an MA at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and doctoral research at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.
